verdict.rationale: Omarchy ships as an installable Arch-based ISO: you write it to a USB stick, answer five questions, and get a finished desktop. Mandatory full-disk encryption fits a whole-disk install that replaces the existing OS. Community users report quick, uncomplicated installs (about 5 minutes on a fresh machine) and daily-driving it as their main OS; one Chromebook user's ISO install failed, but that is a hardware-specific case, not a contradiction of the capability. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of the wipe-and-replace flow (disk selection, overwriting the existing OS) and of migrating data from the old OS, plus broader hardware-compatibility corroboration.
